title: Sliding Shower Doors: Types, Costs, Measuring & Care
h1: Sliding Shower Doors: Frameless vs Framed, Costs, Measuring and Cleaning Guide
description: Compare sliding shower doors: framed, semi-frameless and frameless, glass thickness, typical costs, how to measure and how to clean sliding door tracks.
secondary_keywords: how to clean sliding shower door tracks
excerpt: Framed, semi-frameless or frameless? Compare glass thickness and typical costs, learn to measure your opening and keep sliding door tracks clean.
image_alt: Frameless sliding shower doors with clear glass and a brushed metal top rail over a tiled bathtub
key_takeaways: Sliding (bypass) doors need no swing space, making them ideal for tubs and small bathrooms.
Framed doors use about 1/8–3/16 in. glass, semi-frameless 1/4 in., frameless 5/16–3/8 in.
Typical installed costs run about $400–$1,000 framed, $700–$1,600 semi-frameless and $1,000–$2,500+ frameless.
Measure the width at three heights and buy for the smallest number; check the walls for plumb.
Clean tracks monthly with vinegar and a brush, and squeegee the glass after every shower.

faq.q: Are sliding shower doors better than hinged?
faq.a: Sliding doors are better when floor space is tight or the opening is a bathtub, because they don't swing into the room. Hinged doors are better for narrow walk-in showers with clear floor space in front, since they open fully and have no bottom track to clean. Many apartment bathrooms suit sliding doors best.

faq.q: How thick should glass be for frameless sliding shower doors?
faq.a: Frameless sliding shower doors usually use 5/16 inch or 3/8 inch tempered glass, roughly 8 to 10 millimeters. Thicker glass feels sturdier and resists flexing without a frame. Semi-frameless doors commonly use 1/4 inch glass, and framed doors often use 1/8 to 3/16 inch glass held by the metal frame.

faq.q: How much do sliding shower doors cost installed?
faq.a: Typical installed costs for a standard 60-inch opening are about $400 to $1,000 for a framed door, $700 to $1,600 for semi-frameless and $1,000 to $2,500 or more for frameless. Custom sizes, low-iron or textured glass, protective coatings and premium finishes raise the price, and labor varies by region.

faq.q: How do you clean sliding shower door tracks?
faq.a: Fill the track with white vinegar, or baking soda followed by vinegar, and let it sit 15 to 30 minutes. Scrub corners with an old toothbrush, wipe out the residue with a cloth wrapped around a butter knife, rinse, clear the weep holes and dry the track. Avoid vinegar on natural stone and never mix bleach with vinegar.

faq.q: Can you put a sliding shower door on any bathtub?
faq.a: Most standard alcove tubs with walls on three sides and a flat ledge can take a sliding door. The ledge needs a flat surface for the track, the walls should be within about 3/8 inch of plumb, and the width must fall within the kit's range. Freestanding tubs and very curved ledges usually need a different solution.
